scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: PC0 (20.1.1.x, on the OSPF side) reports it cannot reach
PC12 (120.1.1.x, on the EIGRP side) across the core -- they suspect the OSPF-to-
EIGRP redistribution at R11 broke, or that an interior link on the path is down.
Please confirm the cross-core fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The cross-core path between the OSPF side (PC0, 20.1.1.0/8) and the EIGRP side (PC12, 120.1.1.0/8) is healthy; no redistribution or link fault is present. End-to-end validation shows 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT in both directions between PC0 and PC12. On the OSPF side, R1 has an OSPF-learned route to 120.0.0.0/8 (via 111.1.1.2 on eth1), proving that R11 is successfully injecting EIGRP-learned reachability into OSPF. On the redistribution node R11, the EIGRP route to 120.0.0.0/8 is present (via 112.1.1.2 on eth0), and its OSPF process is explicitly configured to “redistribute eigrp,” confirming the intended policy. On the EIGRP edge, R12 has 120.0.0.0/8 connected on eth1 and a default route to R11 over eth0 (112.1.1.1), allowing return traffic from PC12 to reach OSPF even without specific OSPF prefixes in EIGRP. Hosts are correctly defaulting to their gateways (PC0 via 20.1.1.1; PC12 via 120.1.1.1). Mechanistically, traffic from PC0 to 120/8 follows R1 -> R11 -> R12 -> PC12; return traffic relies on R12’s default back to R11, then to R1. Root cause: no fault found; redistribution and interior links are operating normally. Corrective fix: none required; recommend closing the ticket and monitoring if the report was intermittent.

The agent's logs include an end-to-end reachability test showing 0% loss and route-table evidence of the 120/8 prefix learned via EIGRP on R11 and via OSPF on R1, supporting the conclusion that cross-core reachability is healthy.
